estimate: Large. Option A (carve to a minimal agent-bridge CLI + rebrand): roughly 1.5-2.5 days for someone with the repo loaded — ~120 file deletions, 6 config files edited, 3 parity gates plus 2 skill gates to re-satisfy, snapshot churn in the orchestration preamble tests, and a mandatory packaged Windows smoke because three shims and a pre-lock argv redirect only exercise in a real package. Option B (full delete) is a smaller edit but a larger product decision: it removes multi-agent orchestration and Claude Agent Teams, so budget the same 1.5-2.5 days for the deletion plus separate work to either drop those features cleanly from the UI or rebuild the agent-to-app channel (which reproduces src/cli/runtime/transport.ts). Step 1 — reading reliability-gates.jsonc, max-lines-baseline.txt, .github/, and config/scripts/orca-dev — is ~30 minutes and should be done before committing to either option, since those four files hold the remaining unknowns.
gotchas: Looks like a build target, isn't one. There is NO `cli` entry in electron.vite.config.ts, and config/electron-vite-target.config.ts hard-validates ORCA_ELECTRON_VITE_TARGET against exactly {main, preload, renderer} and throws otherwise. The CLI is built by plain `tsc -p config/tsconfig.cli.json --outDir out`. Do not go looking for a vite cli target to remove — there is none.
build-plugins/plain-node-entry-guard.ts is NOT a CLI coupling. Grep for `cli` in it returns zero hits. The brief listed it as a suspect; it is clear.

`orca` on Linux is the GNOME Orca screen reader at /usr/bin/orca. That single fact is the reason for src/main/cli/linux-bare-orca-dispatcher.ts, src/main/cli/linux-terminal-orca-cli-shim.ts, the `orca-ide` alias, the entire OrchestrationCliCommand union, and a long warning block in skills/orca-cli/SKILL.md. Renaming to `aio-ide` dissolves the collision, so the rebrand lets you DELETE that machinery rather than rename it. This is the one place where the rebrand reduces code instead of just churning it.

`src/main/cli/` and `src/cli/` are different things and only one is the CLI. src/cli/ is the CLI program; src/main/cli/ is the Electron main-process service that installs/registers it. Deleting src/cli/ leaves src/main/cli/ compiling fine while referencing an out/cli/index.js that will never exist (cli-installer.ts:382).

The packaged CLI redirect runs BEFORE the single-instance lock in src/main/index.ts (line 366, lock gate after). Removing the block is fine; reordering the surrounding boot sequence while removing it is how you get a regression where a CLI-shaped launch steals or loses the lock.

asarUnpack in config/electron-builder.config.cjs unpacks out/shared/** and out/main/<agent>/** *because of the CLI* — the CLI is tsc-compiled (not bundled) and runs under ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, which bypasses asar integration entirely, so its cross-directory requires must resolve from app.asar.unpacked. Those unpack rules look like general packaging config but are CLI-motivated; other consumers (daemon-entry.js fork, sherpa-onnx .node addons) motivate only some of the list. Prune with care.

The '!resources/win32{,/**/*}' exclusion in files[] is load-bearing and non-obvious. Its comment cites issue #7351: without it, asarUnpack:['resources/**'] extracts a SECOND orca.cmd to app.asar.unpacked/resources/win32/bin/ with no adjacent orca.exe, and that copy fails to launch. If you rename the shim, keep the exclusion pattern in sync or you resurrect #7351.

src/cli/bundled-skill-guides.ts is generated, and a config/ test imports from it: config/scripts/generate-bundled-skill-guides.test.mjs:5 does `import { BUNDLED_SKILL_GUIDES } from '../../src/cli/bundled-skill-guides'`. So a config/ script test reaches into src/cli — deleting src/cli breaks a test that lives nowhere near it. Also `pnpm lint` (package.json:14) runs verify:bundled-skill-guides, so this fails at lint time, not test time.

4 e2e specs import RuntimeClient from src/cli — they are testing the APP, not the CLI. tests/e2e/{headless-serve-desktop-activation,terminal-tab-close-restart-persistence}.spec.ts use src/cli/runtime/client; tests/e2e/{local-worktree-visibility-runtime-active,orchestration-worker-terminal-visibility}.spec.ts use src/cli/runtime-client. Deleting src/cli costs you app-level coverage, including the orchestration worker-visibility spec. Note there are TWO client modules (src/cli/runtime-client.ts and src/cli/runtime/client.ts) and both are live.

The `claude-agent-teams` TUI agent is an Orca-provided launch mode, not a third-party binary — its detectCmd is literally 'orca'. When you strip 33 agents down to 'Claude Code + Codex', it is easy to keep claude-agent-teams (it says Claude) while deleting the CLI it dispatches through. That combination produces an agent that appears installed only when the CLI shim is on PATH and then fails at launch.

package.json:16 passes literal path args to oxlint: `src config tests mobile`. Deleting mobile/ (already planned) breaks audit:code-quality:native, which runs inside `pnpm lint`. Unrelated to the CLI, but it will surface during CLI verification and waste a debugging cycle.

There are two orca-dev artifacts in config/scripts: orca-dev.mjs (the package.json bin target) and an extensionless `orca-dev` that also references out/cli. Delete/rename both; the extensionless one is easy to miss with a *.mjs glob.
src/main/cli/keyed-promise-queue.ts is a generic utility sitting inside the CLI-service directory. Check for consumers outside src/main/cli/ before deleting the directory wholesale.

orderedSteps: STEP 0 — Decide scope, because the rest branches on it. Option A (recommended): keep a minimal agent-bridge CLI so orchestration + Claude Agent Teams keep working. Option B: full delete, and remove orchestration + agent-teams as product features in the same change. Everything below is written for Option A with Option B deltas called out.

STEP 1 — Finish the three unread inputs before touching anything. `grep -nE 'cli|orchestration' config/reliability-gates.jsonc`; `grep -n 'src/cli' config/max-lines-baseline.txt`; `grep -rnE 'build:cli|typecheck:cli|verify:cli-bin|windows-cli-launcher' .github/`. Also `cat config/scripts/orca-dev` (extensionless file that references out/cli). These four determine which gates fail on delete.

STEP 2 — Establish the keep-set as an explicit list, then prove it compiles. Keep: index.ts, dispatch.ts, args.ts, flags.ts, command-spec.ts, help.ts, format.ts, command-suggestion.ts, selectors.ts, agent-context.ts, shell-command-quote.ts, base64-payload-byte-count.ts, registry-parity.ts, handler-group-manifest.ts, vocabulary-policy.ts, bundled-skill-guides.ts, runtime-client.ts, runtime/** (all), handlers/orchestration.ts, handlers/core.ts, specs/{orchestration.ts,orchestration-worker-specs.ts,core.ts,serve.ts,index.ts} + their .test.ts siblings.

STEP 3 — Delete the feature surface in one commit: src/cli/handlers/{browser-*,computer*,emulator,linear*,vm,project,repo,worktree*,terminal,file,diagnostics,environment,introspection,automations,agent-hooks,skills}.ts, the matching src/cli/specs/*.ts, and the formatters browser-format.ts, browser-handler-groups.ts, computer-format.ts, emulator-logcat-format.ts, emulator-permissions-args.ts, linear-format.ts, linear-request-builders.ts, linear-save-issue-request.ts, project-format.ts, terminal-format.ts, workspace-format.ts, repo-path-arguments.ts, worktree-project-target.ts, codex-command-classification.ts (verify no main-process consumer first), plus every co-located .test.ts.

STEP 4 — Update src/cli/specs/index.ts to stop re-exporting deleted spec modules, then run `pnpm vitest run src/cli/registry-parity.test.ts src/cli/handler-group-manifest.test.ts src/cli/index.test.ts`. These three parity tests are the designed tripwire for spec/handler drift and will name every dangling registration.

STEP 5 — Prune config/tsconfig.cli.json include[]: drop the ~70 per-agent src/main/** entries down to the Claude + Codex ones (agent-hooks/*, claude/*, codex/*, codex-accounts/*, codex-cli/command.ts, rolling-file-backup.ts, runtime/runtime-metadata.ts, win32-utils.ts, agent-state-file-reader.ts). Then `pnpm tc:cli`.

STEP 6 — Prune skills. Delete the triples for orca-emulator, orca-emulator-android, orca-linear, linear-tickets, computer-use (skills/<name>/, skill-guides/<name>.md, skill-stubs/<name>.md). Rewrite skills/orca-cli/SKILL.md + skill-guides/orca-cli.md + skill-stubs/orca-cli.md down to the surviving verbs. Then `pnpm generate:bundled-skill-guides` and `pnpm generate:skill-bundle-manifest` to regenerate src/cli/bundled-skill-guides.ts and the manifest. Verify with `pnpm verify:bundled-skill-guides && pnpm verify:skill-bundle-manifest`.

STEP 7 — Rebrand the binary at the single chokepoint: edit src/shared/orca-cli-command-name.ts (linux 'orca-ide'->'aio-ide', win32 'orca.cmd'->'aio-ide.cmd', default 'orca'->'aio-ide'). Note the linux/darwin split existed only to dodge the GNOME Orca screen-reader collision — with the name `aio-ide` you can collapse all three branches to one string and delete src/main/cli/linux-bare-orca-dispatcher.ts and src/main/cli/linux-terminal-orca-cli-shim.ts (and its call at src/main/ipc/pty.ts:100). That is a real simplification the rename unlocks.

STEP 8 — Propagate the rename through the type + prompt layer: src/main/runtime/orchestration/cli-command.ts (OrchestrationCliCommand union), src/main/runtime/orchestration/preamble.ts (the 'orca-dev' dev-mode literal and the ?? 'orca' fallback), src/shared/tui-agent-config.ts (claude-agent-teams detectCmd/aliases/launchCmd/launchCmdByPlatform), src/main/runtime/claude-agent-teams-shim-env.ts (~/.orca dir, resources/bin/* names, ORCA_AGENT_TEAMS_SHIM_BIN). Run `pnpm vitest run src/main/runtime/orchestration/ src/main/runtime/claude-agent-teams-shim-env` — preamble.test.ts and cli-command.test.ts hold snapshots that will need updating.

STEP 9 — Rename the shipped shims: package.json bin keys (orca->aio-ide, orca-dev->aio-ide-dev), config/scripts/orca-dev.mjs -> aio-ide-dev.mjs, resources/win32/bin/orca.cmd -> aio-ide.cmd, native/windows-cli-launcher/OrcaCliLauncher.cs -> AioIdeCliLauncher.cs with .build/aio-ide.exe. Then update all five coupling sites in config/electron-builder.config.cjs (asarUnpack, the '!resources/win32' files exclusion comment, win extraResources x2, chmodUnixCliLaunchers, deb+rpm afterInstall PATH symlink). Verify with `pnpm verify:cli-bin` and `node --test config/scripts/electron-builder-config.test.mjs` (or however that .mjs test is invoked in this repo).

STEP 10 — Retarget the 4 e2e imports that reach into src/cli for RuntimeClient: tests/e2e/headless-serve-desktop-activation.spec.ts:25 and terminal-tab-close-restart-persistence.spec.ts:14 (src/cli/runtime/client), local-worktree-visibility-runtime-active.spec.ts:17 and orchestration-worker-terminal-visibility.spec.ts:14 (src/cli/runtime-client). Under Option A these paths survive and need no edit; under Option B the RuntimeClient must be relocated (e.g. to src/shared/runtime-client/) or these 4 specs deleted.

STEP 11 — Prune the gate files identified in Step 1: remove deleted src/cli paths from config/max-lines-baseline.txt, remove any CLI entries from config/reliability-gates.jsonc, and drop CLI jobs/steps from .github/ workflows. Also drop the literal `mobile` path from package.json:16 audit:code-quality:native when mobile/ is deleted.

STEP 12 — Full verification in dependency order: `pnpm typecheck` (all three legs), `pnpm lint` (exercises reliability-gates + max-lines-ratchet + both skill gates), `pnpm test`, `pnpm build:cli`, `pnpm build:desktop`. Then a packaged smoke on at least Windows, because the Windows path has three independent shims (orca.cmd, orca.exe native launcher, packaged-cli-entry-redirect) and only a real package exercises them.

STEP 13 (Option B only, in place of steps 2-4 and 7-9) — Full delete. Remove src/cli/, src/main/cli/, src/main/ipc/cli.ts + its preload bridge + renderer 'Install CLI' settings toggle, src/main/startup/{packaged-cli-entry-redirect,appimage-cli-redirect}.{ts,test.ts} and the 5 imports + redirect block in src/main/index.ts:132-133,285-287,366-372, src/main/ssh/ssh-remote-{orca-cli,cli-host-passthrough}.{ts,test.ts}, src/main/runtime/orchestration/ (whole dir) or the preamble path at minimum, the claude-agent-teams entry in src/shared/tui-agent-config.ts + the TuiAgent union member + src/main/runtime/claude-agent-teams-shim-env.ts, src/shared/orca-cli-command-name.ts, native/windows-cli-launcher/, resources/win32/, config/tsconfig.cli.json, config/tsconfig.tc.cli.json, config/scripts/{verify-cli-bin.mjs,verify-cli-bin.test.mjs,install-dev-cli.mjs,orca-dev.mjs,orca-dev,generate-bundled-skill-guides.mjs,generate-bundled-skill-guides.test.mjs}, all 8 skills/skill-guides/skill-stubs triples, and package.json keys bin + scripts {build:cli, tc:cli, typecheck:cli, typecheck:tsc:cli, verify:cli-bin, verify:bundled-skill-guides, generate:bundled-skill-guides, test:repro:remote-agent-session} plus the cli leg of {typecheck, typecheck:tsc, build:desktop, build:release} and the verify:bundled-skill-guides link in `lint`.
risks: Silent orchestration death. Option B removes `orca orchestration send/ask/check` while src/main/runtime/orchestration/preamble.ts still injects those commands into worker prompts. Nothing type-checks this — the prompt is a template string. Workers would run a nonexistent command, never emit worker_done, and the coordinator would report stale-heartbeat failures 10 minutes later with no obvious cause. If you take Option B you must delete the orchestration feature, not just the CLI.

IPC is the wrong replacement for the orchestration channel. The caller is an external agent process (Claude Code / Codex) inside a node-pty, with no preload, no contextBridge, no ipcRenderer. It needs a process-boundary transport — which is precisely src/cli/runtime-client.ts + src/cli/runtime/{transport,websocket-transport,envelope-schema}.ts. Any 'replace with IPC' plan silently re-implements that.

`pnpm build:desktop` and `pnpm build:release` both invoke build:cli (package.json:76,78), and test:repro:remote-agent-session does too (line 27). Removing build:cli without editing these three breaks every build entrypoint at once.

The three parity gates (src/cli/registry-parity.test.ts, handler-group-manifest.test.ts, index.test.ts) fail loudly on partial deletion — that is by design and is your safety net for Step 3. Do not delete or skip them before the prune is complete; they are the only mechanical check that specs, handlers, and the help/manifest surface stay in sync.

config/max-lines-baseline.txt is a ratchet. Entries pointing at deleted files typically hard-error rather than being ignored, so `pnpm lint` breaks on the delete commit until the baseline is pruned in the same change.

Windows has three independent CLI shims that must move together: resources/win32/bin/orca.cmd, the native native/windows-cli-launcher/.build/orca.exe, and the pre-single-instance-lock argv redirect in src/main/startup/packaged-cli-entry-redirect.ts. Renaming or deleting a subset yields the exact silent-GUI-exit failure that issue #7351 and that redirect were written to fix. Unit tests do not catch it; only a packaged run does.

src/main/cli/cli-installer.ts mutates the user's PATH (Windows registry via windows-user-path-registry.ts, /usr/local/bin symlinks on Unix, WSL registrations). Deleting the installer code does not un-install shims already on users' machines. A rebrand-and-ship leaves an orphaned `orca` entry pointing at a path that no longer exists. Ship an uninstall/migration path or accept the orphan knowingly.

deb/rpm afterInstall in config/electron-builder.config.cjs symlinks the CLI onto PATH specifically so `orca-ide serve` works headless, and adds xvfb/xclip as package deps for it. Dropping the CLI without editing that block produces a postinstall that symlinks a nonexistent target.

config/tsconfig.cli.json pulls ~70 individual src/main/** files spanning all 33 agent hook-services. This file couples the CLI deletion to the 33-agents-to-2 strip; doing them in the wrong order produces a long tail of TS2307 module-not-found errors that are tedious to attribute.

src/cli/handlers/codex-command-classification.ts and src/cli/base64-payload-byte-count.ts and src/cli/shell-command-quote.ts look like generic utilities living under src/cli. Grep for main-process consumers before deleting; a wrong call here breaks Codex support, which is one of the two agents you are keeping.

Unverified surfaces: config/reliability-gates.jsonc contents, config/max-lines-baseline.txt contents, .github/ workflow contents, the renderer-side 'Install CLI' settings UI component (I confirmed the IPC handler src/main/ipc/cli.ts but did not locate its React consumer), and the plugin/automations/MCP CLI-shell-out question. I found no evidence of MCP or plugin-API shell-outs to `orca`, but I did not exhaustively grep the plugin host — treat that as open rather than cleared.
summary:
Do NOT delete src/cli/ wholesale. The audit found three in-app features that are hard-wired to the `orca` CLI binary at runtime, and one of them (multi-agent orchestration) cannot be replaced by IPC because the caller is an external agent process (Claude Code / Codex running in a PTY), not the renderer.

Confirmed runtime dependencies:
1. ORCHESTRATION (fatal). `src/main/runtime/orchestration/preamble.ts` builds the dispatch prompt that Orca injects into every worker agent's terminal. That prompt literally instructs the agent to run `orca orchestration send --type worker_done`, `orca orchestration ask`, and `orca orchestration check`. Delete the CLI and workers have no way to report completion — the coordinator's stale-heartbeat check (10 min) fires and every dispatched task fails. `preamble.ts` imports `OrchestrationCliCommand` from `./cli-command`, and `src/main/runtime/orca-runtime.ts:624` calls `resolveTerminalOrchestrationCliCommand`. IPC is not a valid replacement: the consumer is a foreign process in a pty, so it needs the exact socket/WS bridge that `src/cli/runtime-client.ts` + `src/cli/runtime/transport.ts` already implement.
2. CLAUDE AGENT TEAMS (fatal for that launch mode). `src/shared/tui-agent-config.ts` registers the `claude-agent-teams` TUI agent with `detectCmd: 'orca'`, aliases `orca-dev`/`orca-ide`, and `launchCmd: 'orca claude-teams'`. `src/main/runtime/claude-agent-teams-shim-env.ts` writes a `tmux` shim into `~/.orca/claude-agent-teams-bin` whose body is `exec "$ORCA_AGENT_TEAMS_SHIM_BIN" agent-teams-tmux "$@"`. Both resolve through `src/shared/orca-cli-command-name.ts`.
3. SKILLS SHIPPED INTO AGENT PROMPTS. `skills/orca-cli/SKILL.md`, `skill-guides/orca-cli.md`, `skill-stubs/orca-cli.md` plus the `orchestration`, `orca-emulator*`, `orca-linear`, `computer-use` skills document CLI verbs; they are baked into `src/cli/bundled-skill-guides.ts` and gated by `pnpm verify:bundled-skill-guides`. Agents receiving these guides will call commands that no longer exist.
4. `orca serve` headless mode is wired into Linux packaging: `config/electron-builder.config.cjs` deb/rpm `afterInstall` symlinks the shim onto PATH specifically so `orca-ide serve` works on a headless host, and pulls in `xvfb`/`xclip` deps for it.
5. SSH remote: `src/main/ssh/ssh-remote-cli-host-passthrough.ts:75-76` resolves `out/cli/index.js` (asar-unpacked or appPath) to run the CLI on remote hosts.

Two corrections to the brief: (a) there is NO `cli` target in `electron.vite.config.ts` or `config/electron-vite-target.config.ts` — that config only accepts `main|preload|renderer` via `ORCA_ELECTRON_VITE_TARGET`; the CLI is built by plain `tsc -p config/tsconfig.cli.json`. (b) `build-plugins/plain-node-entry-guard.ts` contains zero CLI references (grep for `cli` returned nothing), so it is not a CLI coupling.

RECOMMENDED PLAN: carve, don't delete. Keep a minimal "agent bridge CLI" (~25 files: index/dispatch/args/flags/command-spec/help/format, runtime/*, runtime-client, handlers/orchestration + handlers/core, specs/orchestration + core + serve + index, registry-parity, handler-group-manifest, agent-context, bundled-skill-guides) and delete the ~120 files of feature surface that the Claude-Code+Codex-only product does not need (browser, computer, emulator, linear, vm, project, repo, worktree, terminal, file, diagnostics, environment, introspection, automations, agent-hooks, skills handlers + their specs/formatters). Rebrand the binary `orca`→`aio-ide`. If the product truly must ship with no CLI, orchestration and Agent Teams must be removed as features in the same change — enumerate that as accepted scope loss, not a silent break.
